A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MMSU benchmark. Their main text, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 14 models, human performance, task-level results, and annotated error analyses in Tables 3–4 and Figure 4.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and reports evaluations of 22 models, additional error analyses, and a new noise robustness experiment.

M1.justification: The hierarchical benchmark design, four-stage construction framework, and multiple-choice interface remain the same. Expanded task explanations and annotation documentation do not introduce a new model, learning algorithm, or inference procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation under two Gaussian-noise conditions, extending the tested audio environment. The underlying 5,000-question, 47-task coverage, source datasets, and language coverage documented in the appendices remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds LTU, LTU-AS, SALMONN, MERaLiON2, Baichuan-Audio, Lyra, Phi-4-Multimodal, Baichuan-Omni, and Qwen2.5-Omni-3B, while removing Step-Audio. MiniCPM becomes MiniCPM-O, and the retained Qwen2.5-Omni is identified as the 7B variant. SALMONN was previously cited but not evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 introduces Gaussian noise at half and equal waveform amplitude and evaluates an additional 3B model configuration. Appendix F.2 describes 2–3 annotation-review rounds with reassigned pairs, whereas v1 describes two rounds before expert review; this is a reported procedural revision, not evidence that the dataset was reconstructed. Core evaluation metrics, prompts, and human sample sizes remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained task analysis, v2 adds a four-model noise robustness study and a Qwen2.5-Omni-7B intonation-error case in Figure 5. Table 4 expands the analysis of 300 errors per model from GPT-4o-Audio and Kimi-Audio to include Gemini-1.5-Pro, Qwen2.5-Omni, and DIVA, substantially broadening the diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports model-run seeds, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. Human averaging and error-frequency reporting remain unchanged; additional models and annotation-review rounds do not introduce statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: New Table 3 results include LTU at 22.61%, Lyra at 16.11%, and Qwen2.5-Omni-3B at 56.83%; Step-Audio's 37.42% result is removed. Retained model scores and task plots are unchanged, including Gemini-1.5-Pro's 60.68%. Figure 5 and Table 4 add noise outcomes, a case study, and three models' error breakdowns. Section 3.3 also corrects the perception count from 2,850 to 2,580, matching Table 1 in both versions.

T1.justification: The linguistic foundations remain conceptual rather than mathematical. Neither version supplies formal theorems, proofs, or derivations, and v2's expanded perception-versus-reasoning explanation does not introduce a formal theoretical change.

C1.justification: v2 strengthens the introduction's task-novelty wording from numerous novel tasks within a 47-task benchmark to 47 novel tasks, explicitly calling listed examples unique to MMSU. The central claims about a linguistically grounded benchmark and substantial model–human performance gaps remain intact.

C2.justification: v2 replaces detailed semantic-alignment and transfer-learning explanations with greater emphasis on the human–model perception contrast and overlooked phonological weaknesses, and interprets noise sensitivity as evidence of audio use. It removes v1's limitations concerning recording resources, synthetic speech, incomplete commercial-model testing, and manual filtering. Section 5.4 also incorrectly calls the retained 14.7% refusal rate answer-extraction errors, contradicting Table 4.

D1.justification: Table 3 newly documents model sizes. Appendix F.2 specifies five annotator pairs, 1,000-item assignments, approval by both reviewers, revision and reassignment procedures, and no more than 20 final expert adjustments. These refine existing construction documentation; dataset access, recording details, and generation prompts are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for LTU, Phi-4, Lyra, Baichuan-Omni, and Mathematical Methods in Linguistics, and removes the Step-Audio reference. It emphasizes task uniqueness and underexplored phonological capabilities, while retaining the main related-work organization and benchmark positioning. Citation-style and bibliographic updates are otherwise presentational.

P1.justification: The introduction is substantially reorganized around three benchmark deficiencies, replacing separate contribution bullets with integrated prose. Results interpretations and the human-review appendix are extensively rewritten. v2 also adds an LLM-use disclosure, removes the limitations section, and changes heading and citation styles throughout.

P2.justification: Table 3 is reorganized into model families with a size column and top-two highlighting; Table 4 is transposed and expanded; Table 2 loses its question-type column. A two-panel Figure 5 is added. The document adopts a different template and substantially reflows figures and appendix tables, while retaining the existing task plots, distribution chart, screenshots, and prompt displays.

improvement.justification: The expanded comparisons make MMSU more useful as a model reference, while the explicit paired-review workflow improves readers' ability to assess data quality. New robustness and error analyses add diagnostic value. These gains are tempered by removal of the limitations discussion and the new refusal-versus-extraction reporting error in Section 5.4. With the core benchmark and retained results unchanged, the net improvement is useful but limited.
